record_contract.forms: Representative visible forms or concise system labels for the comparison loop. These make grammatical gender visible where useful but never define gender count by article count.
record_contract.system_type: Lesson-specific classification such as none, two, three, common_neuter, limited, complex, or noun_class_system. Missing data must never be interpreted as no gender.
record_contract.system_badge: Compact learner-facing summary only: ∅, 2, 3, 2+, or N. It does not replace the structured category and agreement data.
record_contract.gender_count: Count of grammatical noun genders only where a stable count is appropriate. Use null for variable/complex systems and broader noun-class systems.
record_contract.gender_categories: Structured categories used by the language where they can be stated defensibly. Broader noun-class systems remain noun classes rather than being relabeled masculine/feminine/neuter.
record_contract.agreement_targets: Places where the classification can surface grammatically, such as articles, adjectives, pronouns, verbs, case, mutation, or noun-class concord. An empty list is valid for languages without productive noun-gender agreement.
record_contract.own_grammar_blurb: Optional learner-facing explanation written in the language itself. Source-language teaching copy is separately complete for all 104 languages under source-copy/.
record_contract.note_en: Short English research note describing the broad learner-facing system without pretending to be an exhaustive grammar.
record_contract.source_refs: One or more research references supporting the language-specific classification. Candidate records remain below human-reviewed trust regardless of the source quality.
record_contract.review_state: Research/editorial workflow state. Candidate records may never self-promote.
record_contract.trust_state: Product confidence stage using the canonical Gef ladder: machine_translated, machine_verified, public, gef_certified.

research_guardrails: Grammatical gender is not a person's gender and does not describe a culture's social gender roles.
Do not infer a gender inventory from article count, language family, script, or a neighboring language.
A language can express natural gender lexically or pronominally without having a productive noun-gender agreement system.
Noun-class systems such as Swahili and Zulu must be represented on their own terms instead of collapsed into masculine/feminine/neuter.
Variable systems such as Norwegian Bokmål use the 2+ badge rather than pretending one fixed gender count covers every standard pattern.
Candidate and machine-translated records require normal language-specific review before promotion.
selection_policy: All 104 canonical learn-from languages have an explicit comparison record. Tier 1 and Tier 2 may additionally become grammar-learning targets only when structured lesson-ready rules exist; Tier 3 remains source/comparison/game support under the current product registry.
